title: New-chat first message lost — panel remounts on lazy conversation create
description:
## Symptom (user-reproduced)

Open a new chat (click "New", or just start typing on a brand-new patient), type the FIRST message, submit → the chat window flashes "Loading conversation…", the message is LOST, and the panel resets. Typing again works. Intermittent-feeling but deterministic given the code path.

## Root cause

`frontend/src/components/chat/ChatPanelWithHistory.tsx:95` keys the ChatPanel on the conversation id:

    key={`${activeConversationId ?? "new"}::${panelMountId}`}

The first send lazily creates the conversation: `ChatPanel.performSend` calls `onConversationCreated(id)` (`ChatPanel.tsx:239`) BEFORE it runs `streamChatMessages` (`ChatPanel.tsx:257`). The parent handler then sets `activeConversationId = id` (`ChatPanelWithHistory.tsx:107`), which changes the key from `new::N` to `<id>::N`. React unmounts the in-flight panel and mounts a fresh one with `conversationId={id}` → `hydrating = Boolean(initialConversationId) = true` → renders "Loading conversation…" (`ChatPanel.tsx:445`) and runs the hydrate effect, which `getConversation`s the just-created, still-EMPTY conversation. The optimistic user/assistant bubbles and the SSE stream belonged to the now-unmounted instance → first message + its response are lost. Second attempt works because `activeConversationId` is already set, so no key change, no remount.

"Brand-new patient, type without clicking New" is the same path: the panel starts at `conversationId=null`, first send creates → remount → loss.

## Fix

Decouple the panel's React `key` (mount identity) from `activeConversationId`:
- Key the ChatPanel on `panelMountId` ONLY. It is already bumped by the user-driven `handleSelect` / `handleNew` — the only moments a true remount is desired.
- `onConversationCreated` should update sidebar highlight (`activeConversationId`) + `listVersion`, but NOT anything in the mount key.
- Guard the hydrate path too: the `conversationId` prop passed to ChatPanel must not flip undefined→id on the LIVE instance, or the `[initialConversationId]` effect (`ChatPanel.tsx:130-165`) re-fires and clobbers in-flight messages via the prop path instead of the key path. Cleanest: track a separate `mountedConversationId` (set only by select/new) for the hydrate prop + key, leaving `activeConversationId` purely for sidebar highlighting.

## Why CI never caught it

The chat E2E (pablo-saas THERAPY-hd4h) is API-only — it hits `/api/chat/*` directly with no browser, so a React remount race is invisible to it. THERAPY-z3a5 (the known flaky chat E2E) is a DIFFERENT race (empty assistant message on SSE timeout in save-as-note), not this.

## Acceptance

- [ ] First message in a new chat persists and streams a response — no "Loading conversation…" flash, no loss
- [ ] Same for "type on brand-new patient without clicking New"
- [ ] Switching to an existing conversation via the sidebar still remounts cleanly (no stale stream)
- [ ] Browser-level regression test added (see related E2E coverage note) — API-only won't catch this
close_reason: Decoupled ChatPanel mount key/hydrate prop from sidebar-highlight state (mountedConversationId vs activeConversationId). Added jsdom+RTL regression test (verified fail-on-bug). Closing with the PR.

title: Document download 401s — <a href> can't send bearer token
description: ## Symptom Clicking a document in the patient Documents list to download it returns **401 (not authenticated)**. No document can be downloaded. ## Root cause \`frontend/src/components/patients/PatientDocuments.tsx:250\` renders the download as a plain anchor: \`\`\`tsx Download \`\`\` which points at \`/api/documents/{id}/file\` (\`frontend/src/lib/api/patientDocuments.ts:107\`). That backend route (\`backend/app/routes/patient_documents.py:405\`, \`download_document_file\`) is gated by \`Depends(require_baa_acceptance)\` — it needs the Firebase **bearer token** in the \`Authorization\` header. A raw \`\` navigation only sends cookies, never custom headers, and Pablo auth is bearer-token (not cookie-session). So the request arrives unauthenticated and 401s before the route can mint the signed GCS URL and 302 to it. The signed-URL design implicitly assumed the browser would hit \`/file\` authenticated; with header-based auth, link navigation can't. ## Fix options 1. **Return the signed URL as JSON, open it client-side (recommended).** Add/adjust the route to return \`{ url: }\` with 200 (or keep the 302 and add a JSON sibling). Frontend calls it through the authenticated fetch client (bearer token attached), then \`window.open(url)\` / \`location.assign(url)\` to the GCS signed URL directly. The signed URL itself needs no auth header — GCS authorizes via the signature — so this cleanly separates app-auth from object-auth. Audit event still fires server-side when the URL is minted. 2. Fetch \`/file\` with \`redirect: \"manual\"\`, read the \`Location\` header, then navigate. Riskier: forwarding the Authorization header into a cross-origin GCS redirect can make GCS reject the request; manual redirect handling across origins is fiddly. 3. Cookie-session auth for this one endpoint — rejected, diverges from the app's bearer-token model. Recommend option 1. ## Relationship to patient-ux-refactor epic The planned \`DocumentViewerSheet\` (design/patient-ux-refactor.md, Phase 1) loads the same signed-URL path to render PDFs/images inline. It MUST use the authenticated-fetch-then-open pattern from option 1, not a raw URL. **This bead is effectively a prerequisite for the viewer bead** — fix the download contract first, then the viewer reuses it. ## Acceptance - [ ] Clicking Download on a document returns the file, not a 401 - [ ] Works for all three categories (chart, therapist_private, psychotherapy_notes) - [ ] The patient-document-access audit event still fires server-side - [ ] Frontend obtains the signed URL via the authenticated API client (bearer token), then navigates to GCS - [ ] No token ever placed in a URL/query string
notes: PR #281 (claude/47h-document-download-signed-url) — /file returns {url} JSON, frontend fetches via authenticated client then navigates to signed GCS URL. Close on merge.
close_reason: Merged in #281 — /file returns signed URL as JSON, frontend fetches authenticated then navigates to GCS.

title: Per-tenant alembic fan-out is not thread-safe — default to serial
description:
`backend/app/db/migrate_tenants.fan_out` parallelizes `command.upgrade` calls across N tenant schemas using a ThreadPoolExecutor (default 8 workers). Alembic's EnvironmentContext is a process-global singleton, so concurrent calls into `command.upgrade` race on it — the second thread to call `context.configure` corrupts the first's state.

Symptom: no-op fan-out runs (every tenant already at head) pass cleanly, hiding the bug indefinitely. The first multi-tenant DDL after the parallelism was enabled fails on every tenant at once — observed today against ~19 schemas during the patient_documents OCR column migration. Serializing with `PABLO_MIGRATE_MAX_WORKERS=1` makes it pass.

Compounding the diagnosis: alembic's env.py calls `fileConfig()` at import, which wipes the root logger's handlers each time it runs. The per-tenant `logger.info`/`logger.exception` output never made it to Cloud Logging — only stdout `print()` calls did. Whatever path eventually re-enables parallelism should also fix this so the next failure is diagnosable on first occurrence.

Default flipped to 1 in the meantime. To re-enable parallelism safely, options worth exploring:
- Subprocess-per-tenant (each child has its own EnvironmentContext)
- Run alembic offline (`--sql`) per tenant and apply DDL ourselves
- Replace alembic at the fan-out layer with a thinner runner that drives migration scripts directly without context globals

Acceptance: fan-out can run with > 1 worker against multiple tenants with real DDL without context corruption. Per-tenant tracebacks surface in Cloud Logging on failure.

title: Doc upload as chat context source — SOURCE_KEY_PATIENT_DOCUMENTS in bundler
description:
Integrate patient_documents with chat_context_bundler so uploaded documents become a selectable source for chat queries, pre-visit brief generation, and letter generation.

Motivation: prescribers and therapists frequently keep prior chart history in another EHR and upload PDFs into Pablo for reference. Without those documents bundled into chat context, chat answers 'I don't know' on any patient whose chart history lives in a PDF. The bundler infrastructure exists (chat_context_bundler.py:53-73) but no SOURCE_KEY_PATIENT_DOCUMENTS.

Scope:
- Add SOURCE_KEY_PATIENT_DOCUMENTS = 'patient_documents' to chat_context_bundler.V1_SOURCE_KEYS.
- Loader that pulls N most recent (or explicitly selected) patient_documents rows by document_id and returns extracted_text as a context section.
- Document the source in patient-context-chat-oss.md §7.1.
- Wire into pre-visit brief default context bundle.
- Wire into letter generator default context bundle.
- Token-budget honoring (long documents truncate per existing rules).

Acceptance: bundler accepts patient_documents as a source; pre-visit brief incorporates document content; letter generator can reference document content; truncation works for large documents; audit log captures which documents were included in each bundle.

title: Patient list has no pagination — UI caps at 20 rows
description:
## Problem

\`PatientTable.tsx\` calls \`usePatientList({ search })\` with no \`page_size\` and no \`page\` controls. The backend default is \`page_size=20\` (\`backend/app/routes/patients.py:163\`), so the UI silently truncates to the first 20 patients sorted by last_name, first_name. There is no Next/Prev, no \"showing N of M\", and no way for a clinician with 21+ patients to reach the rest of their roster except by typing into the search box.

The backend response already returns \`total\` alongside \`data\` (\`PatientListResponse\`), so the data is there — the UI just discards it.

## Why it matters

For solo therapists this caps usable size at 20 active clients. As soon as one provider has more — totally normal for an established practice — they cannot see their full list without searching by name (which has its own UX issues, see [[patient-search-needs-improvement]]).

## Options

1. **Add pagination controls.** Standard Prev/Next + page indicator. Honest \"showing 1-20 of N\" framing. Minimal change.
2. **Increase the default page_size + infinite scroll.** Friendlier on small lists. More work, but matches how the table feels for someone with 35 patients.
3. **Increase the default page_size to 100 and call it a day.** API max is already 100; cheapest fix. Caps later instead of at 20.

Recommendation: option 3 short-term (one-line fix: \`usePatientList({ search, page_size: 100 })\`), then revisit pagination/infinite-scroll if any practice grows past 100.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A user with >20 patients can see them all in the UI
- [ ] Page shows the actual \`total\` somewhere so users know what they're looking at
- [ ] Tests cover the chosen page_size
close_reason: Patient list: page_size=100 + 'Showing N of M' total (y93); substring search across both names, search_by toggle dropped, generic placeholder (bgr). Closing with the PR.

title: Grant documentai.apiUser to prod backend SA
description:
## Problem

On 2026-05-24 we wired the Document AI OCR processor into Cloud Run for both pablohealth-dev and pablohealth-prod. Dev is fully functional. **Prod backend SA does not have \`roles/documentai.apiUser\`**, so when the OCR fallback fires it will get an auth-denied error from the Document AI API instead of successfully OCR'ing.

The Cloud Run env vars are already set on prod (revision pablo-backend-00249-qcp) — only the IAM grant is missing. Dev's backend SA already has this role, which is why dev works.

## Why this wasn't done automatically

Cross-environment IAM-modifying gcloud commands are blocked in the Claude Code harness on prod targets. The dev grant was done manually before the deploy; prod's was missed.

## The one-liner

\`\`\`bash
gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding pablohealth-prod \\
  --member=serviceAccount:pablo-backend@pablohealth-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com \\
  --role=roles/documentai.apiUser \\
  --condition=None
\`\`\`

## Verify

After granting, upload a scanned PDF in prod and confirm the \"OCR not yet supported\" badge doesn't appear on the document row.

## Acceptance

- [ ] \`gcloud projects get-iam-policy pablohealth-prod\` shows pablo-backend SA with documentai.apiUser
- [ ] Scanned PDF upload in prod produces extracted_text (visible via patient document detail endpoint or chat citation manifest)
close_reason: IAM grant applied to pablohealth-prod by user; verified pablo-backend@pablohealth-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com now has roles/documentai.apiUser. Prod OCR fully wired.

title: Persist title and credentials on PATCH /me; surface in /me/status
description:
PATCH /api/users/me accepts display_name, title, and credentials in the request schema but only persists display_name. title and credentials are profile fields on ClinicianProfile (per-tenant) and get silently dropped today (see backend/app/routes/users.py:259 inline comment).

Scope:
- PATCH /api/users/me: when title and/or credentials are present, upsert them onto the calling user's ClinicianProfile row (create-if-missing, tenant-scoped via current tenant context). Same auth posture as the existing display_name update — title and credentials are profile metadata, not PHI.
- GET /api/users/me/status: include title and credentials in the response payload alongside the existing fields.
- Update the inline comment at users.py:259 to reflect the actual behavior.

The fields are already accepted by the request schema; the bug is they don't round-trip through persistence.

title: Simplify chat source selection — drop unavailable sources, fix 'Selected sessions', add document picker
description:
## Problem

The chat source-chip rail (frontend/src/components/chat/SourceChipRail.tsx + sourceMeta.ts) exposes 10 sources, but most aren't usable today, so the UI reads as complex while doing little:

- **'Selected sessions' (progress_notes_explicit) is broken.** Toggling the chip sets the key to boolean `true` (ChatPanel.handleAddSource/handleToggleSource), but the backend loader requires `{note_ids:[...]}` (backend/app/services/chat_context_bundler.py:441) and raises InvalidSelectionError otherwise. There is no session-picker UI to supply note_ids. Net: selecting it does nothing useful or errors the turn. This is the user-reported "doesn't appear to do anything."
- **'Uploaded documents' (patient_documents) is all-or-nothing.** Toggling includes EVERY uploaded document. The backend already supports an explicit `ids` list (_load_patient_documents falls back to all-for-patient only when no ids given, chat_context_bundler.py:~569), but there's no UI to pick which documents.
- **Always-empty sources clutter the rail.** most_recent_intake, treatment_plan_active, safety_plan_active, current_medications reference note types (intake/treatment_plan/safety_plan/medications) not registered in the OSS note-type registry — only soap + narrative ship today (see comment chat_context_bundler.py:25-31). They always return row_count=0 / reason=no_data. lab_values_recent + vitals_recent have no data path in a therapy product.
- The "+ Add source" menu only hides sources flagged `module_not_available` in the latest manifest, and only AFTER the first turn — so on a fresh chat all 10 show.

## Asks

1. **Surface only sources with a working data path** in the chip rail + add-source menu: progress_notes_recent, patient_documents, pasted_text. Keep the backend loaders for the not-yet-registered note types (they're forward-compatible) but don't show chips for them until their note types actually ship.
2. **Remove the 'Selected sessions' chip** (progress_notes_explicit) for now — it's broken without a picker. If per-session selection is wanted later, file a follow-up to build a note-multiselect that supplies `note_ids` in the correct shape.
3. **Add a per-document picker** for patient_documents so the clinician can choose which uploaded documents to include (backend already supports the `ids` shape). Ties into the patient-documents UI work in this epic (PABLO-6x5.5).
4. Result: a short, honest source rail where every visible source works.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Source rail + add menu show only sources with a real data path (no always-empty chips on a fresh chat)
- [ ] No visible source can produce an InvalidSelectionError from a boolean-vs-shape mismatch
- [ ] 'Selected sessions' removed (or a working picker added)
- [ ] Uploaded documents can be included selectively, not only all-or-nothing

title: Patient search: clarify field + add substring match + expose first-name search
description:
## Problem

Three related UX gaps in the patient list search input (\`PatientTable.tsx:139\`):

1. **No indication search is last-name**. Placeholder says \"Search patients by name...\". The backend defaults \`search_by=last_name\` (\`backend/app/routes/patients.py:160\`), so typing a first name returns nothing — silently. Users assume their patient was deleted or the list is broken.

2. **Prefix-only matching**. The repo uses \`first_name_lower.startswith(search_lower)\` / \`last_name_lower.startswith(search_lower)\` (\`backend/app/repositories/patient.py:206-208\`). \"smith\" matches Smith; \"mith\" does not. Most users expect substring search (\"contains\"), especially when they remember the middle of a hyphenated last name or only a fragment.

3. **\`search_by\` query param is exposed in the API but never in the UI**. The route accepts \`search_by=first_name|last_name\` but \`usePatientList\` callers never pass it. There's no toggle, no dropdown, no smart heuristic (\"if input has a comma, split into last, first\").

## Options

**Minimum viable improvement:**
- Update placeholder to \`\"Search by last name...\"\` so the contract is honest
- Add a small \"First name\" toggle next to the search input

**Better:**
- Change \`startswith\` to \`contains\` (i.e., \`%search%\`) — substring match in both fields by default, no toggle needed. Repo + tests change in one place. Trade-off: substring on a large patient list is slower than prefix, but with the ILIKE pattern and lower-cased indexed columns it's fine through low-thousands rows.
- Drop the \`search_by\` param entirely; always search both fields.

**Best:**
- Substring search across \`first_name || ' ' || last_name\` so \"john smi\" works
- Optional: weight last-name matches higher in ranking
- Keep input copy as \"Search patients...\"

## Recommendation

Go directly to \"Better\" — substring search both fields, drop \`search_by\` toggle. It's the smallest change that produces the least surprising behavior. \"Best\" can follow if users still complain about full-name search.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Typing a middle fragment of a last name finds the patient (substring match)
- [ ] Typing a first name finds the patient (without any toggle)
- [ ] Placeholder text either matches actual behavior or behavior is broadened to match the generic placeholder
- [ ] Repo + route tests updated
close_reason: Patient list: page_size=100 + 'Showing N of M' total (y93); substring search across both names, search_by toggle dropped, generic placeholder (bgr). Closing with the PR.

title: Auto-derive Document AI project + processor at startup
description:
## Problem

The Document AI OCR client (\`backend/app/services/document_ai_ocr.py\`) gates on three env vars: \`DOCUMENT_AI_PROJECT_ID\`, \`DOCUMENT_AI_PROCESSOR_ID\`, \`DOCUMENT_AI_LOCATION\`. If any are unset, \`is_configured\` returns False, OCR silently falls back to \"unavailable\", and finalized scanned PDFs show \"OCR not yet supported — text extraction failed\" in the UI.

This is exactly how the feature broke when the OCR processors were provisioned in pablohealth-dev and pablohealth-prod on 2026-05-24 — the processors exist, the IAM role is granted (in dev), but no one wired the env vars into Cloud Run. The deploy isn't atomic, so we shipped a half-configured feature.

## Why most of this is redundant

1. **\`DOCUMENT_AI_PROJECT_ID\`** is always the same as the running GCP project. Cloud Run already injects \`GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT\` automatically (also \`GCP_PROJECT_ID\` in our config). \`google.auth.default()\` returns the project too. Asking operators to set this third copy is pure ceremony.

2. **\`DOCUMENT_AI_PROCESSOR_ID\`** is less trivially redundant — a project can hold many processors (OCR, Form Parser, Handwriting, etc.) — but in practice we always want \"the processor whose displayName is \`pablo-patient-doc-ocr\`\". That's discoverable at startup via \`processors.list\` with a name filter, cached for the lifetime of the process.

3. **\`DOCUMENT_AI_LOCATION\`** can default to \"us\" (where our processors live) and only be overridden if we ever need EU.

## Proposed change

In \`DocumentAiOcrClient\`:
- If \`document_ai_project_id\` is None, fall back to \`os.environ.get(\"GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT\")\` then \`google.auth.default()[1]\`.
- If \`document_ai_processor_id\` is None, on first call run \`processors.list(parent=...)\` filtered by displayName (constant \`PABLO_OCR_PROCESSOR_NAME = \"pablo-patient-doc-ocr\"\`); cache the resolved id on the instance.
- Log once at startup with the resolved values so it's obvious in logs which processor is being used.
- Keep the env vars as escape hatches for tests and local overrides.

Outcome: zero-config OCR in any environment where a processor exists with the canonical name. Provisioning becomes \"create the processor + grant the IAM role\" — no Cloud Run env-var update step.

## Acceptance

- [ ] OCR works in pablohealth-dev with no DOCUMENT_AI_* env vars set
- [ ] Tests still pass with explicit env vars (escape hatch preserved)
- [ ] Startup log shows the resolved project + processor id once
- [ ] Doc string on \`DocumentAiOcrClient\` updated to describe the resolution order

title: [epic] Patient document import — capability expansion
description:
Parent epic for OSS-side enhancements to the Document AI OCR fallback (commit 5ba5d1b). Groups capability work across four themes:

A. Structured field extraction (Form Parser):
   - PABLO-1oi Form Parser invocation in DocumentAiOcrClient
   - PABLO-g50 FormField → outcome-measure schema mapping helpers
   - PABLO-o5k outcome_measures destination table

B. Processor variety:
   - PABLO-tz6 Handwriting OCR processor support

C. Upload UX:
   - PABLO-e6c Bulk upload UI for multi-file intake batches
   - PABLO-dvv Document-type tagging at upload time
   - PABLO-t7c Auto-categorize uploaded documents by content

D. Scale:
   - PABLO-q3d Async OCR pipeline for documents > 30 pages

Each child bead describes a generic capability. Processor IDs, field-to-schema mappings, and deployment-specific configuration are intentionally outside the engine — each deployment provides its own.

title: Async OCR pipeline for documents > 30 pages
description: Document AI's synchronous OCR endpoint has a 30-page limit. Documents exceeding it currently fail extraction. Add an async batch-processing path: queue the document, kick off Document AI batch operation, poll for completion, store the result. Long-document upload UX shows a 'processing' state until the async job completes.

title: Handwriting OCR processor support
description:
Document AI exposes a handwriting-optimized OCR processor distinct from the default text processor. Add it as a selectable processor type in DocumentAiOcrClient. Default OCR processor produces poor results on handwritten notes; FQHCs and any practice receiving paper intakes need the handwriting variant.

Capability only — processor ID selection is configurable per-deployment.

title: FormField → outcome-measure schema mapping helpers
description:
Generic helper that maps Document AI FormField key/value entries into structured outcome-measure rows. The mapper itself is content-agnostic — it takes a schema definition (field labels, value parsers, score aggregation rules) and FormField entries, and returns parsed records.

Schema definitions are supplied per-deployment.

title: outcome_measures destination table
description: New OSS clinical-chart table for storing scored instruments (PHQ-9 total + per-item, GAD-7 total + per-item, generic instrument rows). Joined to patient_id + appointment_id, displayed in chart UI alongside vitals/notes. Lives in OSS because the score data belongs in the chart regardless of where the underlying form came from (manual entry, OCR extraction, patient portal).

title: Form Parser invocation in DocumentAiOcrClient
description:
Extend DocumentAiOcrClient to call Document AI Form Parser processors (structured field extraction) in addition to the existing OCR processor. Form Parser returns FormField entries (key/value pairs) instead of plain text — needs a different response-shape handler but shares ~95% of the existing client code (auth, project/location resolution, retry, error handling).

Generic capability — processor ID and field schemas are configured per-deployment.

title: Document-type tagging at upload time
description: Add a doc_type column to patient_documents with a defined enum (intake, lab, imaging, letter, prior_records, consent, other). Required field at upload (UI dropdown). Enables filtering, downstream auto-categorization (separate bead), and chart-UI grouping.

title: Bulk upload UI for multi-file intake batches
description: Frontend drag-drop / file-picker that accepts multiple files at once and creates a patient_documents row per file. Currently the upload UI is one-file-at-a-time. Common case: intake packet arrives as 5–10 PDFs that all attach to the same patient. Backend already supports concurrent uploads; this is purely a frontend UX change.

title: Auto-categorize uploaded documents by content
description: LLM-assisted classification of patient_documents into doc-type buckets (intake form, lab result, prior records, letter, image, other) based on extracted text. Pre-fills the doc-type field at upload; user can override. Reduces filing friction for the common case where a folder of scans needs sorting.
